title: 503 Service Unavailable
description: Resolve temporary 503 responses — maintenance mode, overloaded server, or security plugins blocking traffic.

steps.title: Check for .maintenance File
steps.instructions: Delete .maintenance in the WordPress root if a failed update left the site in maintenance mode. The file should auto-remove after 10 minutes — stale files cause 503.

steps.title: Disable Maintenance Mode Plugins
steps.instructions: Deactivate plugins that put the site in maintenance or coming-soon mode. Check wp-content/maintenance.php and hosting-level maintenance toggles.

steps.title: Review Server Load and Rate Limits
steps.instructions: High traffic or DDoS can trigger 503 from the host or WAF. Check resource graphs, enable rate limiting, and contact support if the server is at capacity.

steps.title: Audit Security Plugin Lockouts
steps.instructions: Wordfence, iThemes, or server mod_security rules may return 503 for blocked IPs. Whitelist your office IP and review recent firewall blocks.

steps.title: Bypass or Purge Caching Layer
steps.instructions: A misconfigured page cache or CDN can serve stale 503 pages. Purge all caches and test with cache bypass (nocache query param or development mode).

steps.title: Confirm Public Access Restored
steps.instructions: Test from an external network and incognito browser. Verify crawlers and monitoring tools receive HTTP 200 on key URLs.
